ns2:course.label: Industrial Heritage and Communities
ns2:course.description: Primarily examines the legacy of the Industrial Revolution in the United Kingdom and the United States where former industrial sites (such as textile mills, coal mines, chocolate factories) have been transformed from abandoned ruins into major tourist attractions, economic regeneration machines for their communities, and even UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Studies industrial places in the context of the times in which they were operating and the processes by which they have been repurposed.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Social & Beh Sci - Soc Sci course.
